messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Hosted API p95/p99 latency spike detected for production cluster prod-eu-1 — queue depth rising. metric: request_queue_length >= 2500 for 2m :rotating_light:
incident-bot: Details: p95=980ms -> 3.2s, p99=1.8s -> 12.6s, error rate (5xx) increased from 0.02% -> 1.3% in last 5m. Autoscaler failed to scale beyond 40 instances (cap hit).
sara (oncall): acked. I'm looking now. where's load coming from? any deploys?
ajay (sre): I see a traffic spike from a handful of customer keys, sudden sustained QPS increase ~ 6x baseline, mostly short-chat completions. No recent deploys in last 30m.
mia (serving): Confirmed: GPU pool gpu-prod-eu-1 hit node limit. Autoscaler attempted scale but returned `quota_exceeded` errors from cloud provider at 03:42:11Z. Kernel packing queue grew and batching latency ballooned.
sara (oncall): ok. Priority: reduce customer impact quickly. Proposed mitigation options: 1) enable rate limit shed for top noisy keys 2) turn on fallback model variant on CPU for non-latency-critical traffic 3) increase autoscale cap (if provider allows) 4) failover some traffic to dedicated pools if available. Thoughts?
ajay (sre): Agree. Start with targeted rate limiting + fallback model. We can also stale-route to lower-cost model to reduce GPU usage.
kevin (infra): I've requested quota increase but provider says manual approval may take 30+m. We have spare Dedicated capacity in dedicated-eu-1 pool with reserved GPUs — can we spillover there?
mia (serving): Yes, we have dedicated-eu-1 with compatible kernels. Need to update routing policy to allow dedicated fallback for tier=standard. That requires a quick config flip in routing service.
sara (oncall): on it. I'll make the config change to allow fallback to dedicated-eu-1 for standard tier. Doing a canary 5% -> 25% -> 100%.
ops-bot: ACTION: routing-config updated by sara (oncall) — added fallback route to dedicated-eu-1 for tier=standard. Canary set to 5%.
ajay (sre): I'll start applying targeted rate limits to the top 10 noisy API keys. Share keys?
lucy (customer-ops): I can DM the list of customer support cases experiencing timeouts. We should avoid blocking paying enterprise customers. Need to exempt certain orgs.
sara (oncall): good call. ajay, apply soft throttles on noisy keys (token-rate decrease) and exempt enterprise-* orgs.
ajay (sre): done. Applied token-based throttling: top 10 keys limited to 30% of previous burst capacity. Monitoring impact.
mi a (serving): (note: typo) — mia: Routing canary at 5% is healthy so far. GPU queue length decreased from 2600 -> 1800 in 4m. p95 dropped to ~2s.
incident-bot: NOTE: routing canary increased automatically to 25% after 5m (policy: canary-autoscale).
sara (oncall): bump to 50% canary, continue.
ops-bot: ACTION: routing-config updated by sara (oncall) — canary at 50%.
ajay (sre): With throttles + routing, queue down to 900. p95 ~1.2s, p99 ~4.1s. Error rate still ~0.6% from backend timeouts.
kevin (infra): Dedicated spillover is using reserved GPUs; throughput per-GPU slightly lower for fallback but stable. We should still pursue quota request in parallel.
lucy (customer-ops): Notifying top affected customers: sent initial alert to subset, have outbound template ready — minimal impact message explaining throttling and mitigation.
sara (oncall): Good. Next: enable model fallback for non-critical endpoints (embeddings and non-stream chat) to CPU variant to relieve GPU pressure. Mia, can you roll that?
mia (serving): I'll toggle fallback flag for non-stream routes now. ops-bot will run a deploy job.
ops-bot: DEPLOY: toggled fallback-models for routes: /v1/embeddings, /v1/completions-nonstream. Job id: deploy-2025-06-04-1112.
ajay (sre): after deploy, additional load moved off GPUs. Queue now ~420. p95 ~700ms, p99 ~1.9s. Error rate down to 0.15%. Looks stable.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: pressure relieved. Autoscaler still showing cap hit for a subset of nodes; quota request pending.
sara (oncall): I'm going to start an incident bridge to track follow-ups (root cause + quota). Can someone take postmortem? ajay?
ajay (sre): I can own the postmortem. Will capture timeline, decisions, and remediation: - improve autoscaler awareness of provider quota errors - add preemptive spillover when queue > 1000 - add per-key burst mitigation auto-playbooks.
lucy (customer-ops): I'll follow up with affected customers with a post-incident note once root cause is confirmed.
kevin (infra): Action items for infra: request higher region GPU quota, add alert for `autoscaler_quota_errors` separate from general scale failures.
sara (oncall): Handing over to ajay for deep dive. I'll stay available for any followups. Handoff to ajay (sre) at 03:52Z.
ajay (sre): taking over. Creating incident doc in /incidents/1748123456. I'll add timeline and raw metrics.
incident-bot: INCIDENT: Status changed to mitigated by sara (oncall) — followups assigned.
ops-bot: REMINDER: next on-call rotation in 6h: mark for follow-up and add to rotation notes.
mi a (serving): (typo correction) mia: adding logs and a snippet of the autoscaler error: ```json
{"error":"quota_exceeded","region":"eu-west-1","requested_nodes":10,"available_nodes":0}
```
ajay (sre): saved. will include that in postmortem. Closing thread once doc is posted.
